key_insight: Hybrid quantum-inspired CNNs do not universally beat classical CNNs, but they can outperform them in intermediate-data regimes while remaining similarly explainable.
engineering_relevance: For medical image classification, the best architecture depends on training set size and simulation cost, so quantum-inspired components should be chosen only when they offer a clear accuracy or scalability tradeoff.
method: Compared a hybrid quantum-inspired CNN against a parameter-matched classical CNN with only one intermediate dense layer changed.
Tested both models on two real medical datasets across varied hyperparameters for a fair, dataset-independent benchmark.
Added SHAP-based comparison metrics, |SHAP|IoU and EMD_pos, to assess whether both models attend to plausible anatomical regions.
evidence_signal: Across systematic evaluations, the HQiCNN achieved its strongest gains with intermediate-sized training sets, while the classical CNN reached the best accuracies on the largest datasets; both showed anatomically plausible attention.
watch_item: Emulated quantum circuits can be computationally expensive to simulate, and removing entanglement may improve scalability even if it changes model expressivity.
paper_title: Do emulated quantum circuits change what CNNs look at? Performance and explainability comparison in medical image classification
